final_answer: Depth-first search (dfs) explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking, using a stack. It quickly finds a path but might miss the shortest one. Breadth-first search (bfs) explores all neighbors level by level, using a queue, ensuring the shortest path in unweighted graphs. Choose dfs for space efficiency or cycle detection; choose bfs for shortest path problems.
